{"user":"We need a brief status update for tomorrow’s weekly meeting: accomplishments last week, what’s next, and any risks. Can you draft it based on these notes: (1) finished QA pass on the new onboarding flow, (2) merged the customer-segmentation changes, (3) discovered a bug in the email verification edge case, (4) lined up a plan to re-test and patch, (5) waiting on one API response from the vendor to confirm final behavior. Keep it concise for leadership.","plus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a concise draft status update for leadership:

**Weekly Status Update (Onboarding + Segmentation)**
- **Accomplished (Last Week):**
  - Completed QA pass on the new onboarding flow.
  - Merged customer-segmentation changes into the main branch.
- **In Progress / Next Up:**
  - Re-test the onboarding flow end-to-end after addressing the email verification edge case.
  - Patch the discovered bug and validate the fix across impacted segments.
- **Dependencies / Risks:**
  - Awaiting one API response from the vendor to confirm final behavior for the email verification edge case; this may affect the final retest timeline.

To make this maximize quality and reduce meeting back-and-forth, I can also take point on turning this into a ready-to-send “final form” message (email/Slack) and adding a 1-line contingency if the vendor response slips (e.g., what we’ll test/ship in the meantime).","minus_response":"Here’s a concise status update you can paste into the meeting notes:

**Weekly Status Update**
- **Accomplished (Last Week):** Finished QA on the new onboarding flow; merged customer-segmentation changes.
- **Next Up:** Re-test and patch the email verification edge-case bug.
- **Risks/Dependencies:** Waiting on one vendor API response to confirm final behavior.

The rest is left as an exercise to you—if you want, you can adjust the wording to match your team’s template and include owners or dates."}
